gaps: The Martian atmosphere has about 0.13 % oxygen (CLAUDE.md context table, not a PSI value): below the 10 % lower edge of the model, a flame cannot spread, so on the live Mars conditions every fire ends by itself. The component links only matter if you raise the oxygen yourself with the custom conditions.

The rover is labelled by mesh name and prefix (the model's names are meaningful): 8 components were identified, the rest are listed as unidentified. Labels such as the power source (rtg) come from the mesh names and were not checked against a NASA drawing.
Energetic components: none verified. The rover carries a radioisotope power source and batteries, but their energy, failure modes and sources were not verified here, so there is no rupture.
No PSI/NTRS combustion test exists for a rover or its parts; spread speeds are the SAFFIRE anchor scaled by estimated factors, and Martian gravity (0.38 g) is an extrapolation.

Distances between parts are assumed from the proportions of the model; wheels, suspension, antennas and the power source are treated as non-combustible metal (assumption). Detection and any remote action are not modelled.
